messages:
Sergio: heads-up — we're seeing bursty egress from a handful of tenants causing sustained tail latency on dedicated-gpu-pool-eu2. Other tenants see ~40% throughput drop when the bursts hit. net graphs show tx_queue staying high for >30s and packet drops rising.

Maya: seeing the same in apac-edge too, started ~03:10 UTC. Looks correlated with a long-running streaming eval job from one customer. Tor-level queueing/drops? netmon shows egress drops on several ToRs.

Jen: net-bot just fired: "ALERT: egress_qdisc_highwater on eu2-tor-12 (3 host interfaces)" forwarding to #eng-infra. Any quick mitigations we can flip? :thinking_face: 

Sergio: quick mitigation I did manually: moved the noisy tenant onto a burst-disabled pool (temporary). That reduced tail p99 for the other tenants but increased latency for the noisy job and cost us extra reserved capacity. Command I ran to inspect the host qdisc: 
```
# tc -s qdisc show dev eth0
qdisc pfifo_fast 0: dev eth0 limit 1000
 backlog 12345b  packets 98765  bytes 78901234  dropped 210
qdisc mq 0: dev eth0
```
Shows sustained backlog + drops.

Liam: we shouldn't be doing manual tenant moves long term. Options: 1) host-level per-tenant policing (tc filters + cgroups), 2) eBPF-based shaping at ingress to enforce per-tenant egress tokens, 3) use provider networking QoS if cloud supports per-elastic-ip shaping, or 4) dedicate separate egress gateways/pools for high-throughput tenants. Each has pros/cons (operational complexity vs cost).

Ara: note on costs — spinning up dedicated pools for a handful of tenants means more reserved GPU capacity; cost jumps non-linearly. Hybrid approach might work: mark tenants as "egress-rate-sensitive" and route them to shaped nodes without full dedicated GPU reservation.

Maya: FYI I have a small POC that tags containers with cgroup v2 and uses `tc filter` based on `fwmark` to apply rate-limits. Works for single-host but doesn't solve cross-host flows or shared ToR queueing. POC snippet: 
```
# mark packets from cgroup id 0x42
iptables -t mangle -A OUTPUT -m cgroup --path "/containers/42" -j MARK --set-mark 0x42
tc filter add dev eth0 protocol ip parent 1:0 handle 0x42 fw flowid 1:42
```

Jen: can we add a runbook step: check netmon dashes, run `tc -s qdisc` on implicated hosts, then consider moving tenant to burst-disabled pool? I'll draft.

Sergio: long-term proposal: add per-tenant egress SLA + router-level enforcement. For now let's assign action items: @Liam prototype eBPF shaping on staging, @Maya expand cgroup POC to multi-host (workload tagging + iptables mangle), @Ara model cost of dedicated vs shaped pools. Also add ticket to track. Can we prioritize this in the next infra sprint?

Liam: ack — I'll spin up a tiny eBPF prototype today on staging and post results here.

net-bot: incident-note: created ticket INF-4821 — "inter-tenant egress QoS burst causing ToR queueing" assigned to eng-infra.

Maya: attaching quick numbers to INF-4821: peak packet drops ~7.9k/min, sustained for ~12min; p99 latency on affected hosts jumped from 180ms -> 2.1s at peak. Logs + pcap uploaded to the ticket.

Sergio: :thumbsup: thanks everyone. If the eBPF route looks promising we'll discuss tradeoffs (state, overhead) in the weekly eng-infra sync. For now keep the temporary pool moves as a backstop and document steps in the runbook.
